reasoning: Roofline reports compute bottleneck with Compute SOL 89.8% vs Memory SOL 42.1%. Kernel metrics match this: sm__throughput 89.85% of peak sustained elapsed and dram/gpu memory throughput only 42.11%, so performance is limited by arithmetic throughput rather than memory bandwidth.

root_causes.cause: High FP32 vector-ALU intensity from fused FC1 + SiLU + FC2 reductions dominates runtime.

evidence.interpretation: Compute pipeline is already close to peak sustained throughput, indicating ALU-bound execution.

fixes.fix: Increase math throughput per cycle by retuning tile shapes and software pipelining (e.g., try larger BLOCK_J/BLOCK_OUT and higher num_stages if registers allow) to improve ILP and reduce reduction overhead.
fixes.rationale: When compute is the limiter, better instruction scheduling/ILP is the main lever for gaining remaining headroom.

root_causes.cause: Kernel does not use tensor-core/matrix instructions, leaving faster low-precision matrix hardware unused for this GEMM-like workload.

evidence.interpretation: No tensor/matrix pipe utilization; all math is executed on regular vector ALUs.

fixes.fix: Refactor inner products to tensor-core-compatible Triton matmul patterns (block sizes/layouts and datatypes that map to MFMA/WGMMA equivalents on gfx942).
fixes.rationale: Shifting dense dot-product work to matrix hardware can raise peak attainable compute and reduce time in VALU-bound sections.
